insight.title: Underground Fungi Route Forest Resources Using Supply and Demand
insight.subtitle: Operating as a decentralized underground market, mycelium dynamically adjusts resource distribution to keep the entire forest alive.
insight.notificationHook: Underground fungi route resources in real tim

sections.text: Deep beneath the forest floor, fungal threads connect different tree species into a single network. When a shaded tree starves for carbon, neighboring trees send food through these underground lines to save it.

This is not charity, but a highly efficient market. The fungal network acts as a broker, trading soil nutrients for plant sugars, dynamically adjusting the exchange rate based on local scarcity and demand.

Without a central brain, the network prevents any single tree from failing. By balancing resources across the ecosystem, the fungus secures its own food supply and ensures the survival of the entire forest.
An underground economy where resource distribution is perfectly automated.
